discordBridge.intro: A bridge links channels on this server with channels on a Discord server. Messages sent on either side show up on the other, with each sender's name and picture.

start.title: Where should the bridge run?
start.needs: You need a Discord account with the Manage Server permission on the Discord server you want to connect. Setup takes about ten minutes.

hosted.title: Use your own bot, run on this instance
hosted.lead: Create a Discord bot with your own name and avatar and paste its token here; this instance runs it.
hosted.point2: In Discord, the bot carries the name and avatar you give it.
hosted.tradeoff: This instance's operator holds your bot's token and could read any Discord channel the bot can see. Give the bot access only to the channels you bridge.

self.title: Run it yourself
self.point1: Your Discord bot's token stays with you.
self.point2: You run one command (Docker) on any computer that's always on: a home server, a VPS, a Raspberry Pi.
self.tradeoff: The bridge works only while that computer is on and online.

start.hostingUnavailable: This instance doesn't run bridges for its communities, so the bridge runs on a computer of yours.
start.bothWays: Either way, messages in bridged channels pass through this instance like any other message here.

instance.point1: Nothing to create or install: you add the bot to your Discord server in one click.
instance.point2: This instance runs the bridge for you.

bot.optionsLead: These two options decide which switches you need. You can change them later; the list above follows.
bot.save: Click {save} at the bottom of the page.

bot.hostedAccess: You'll paste it into this page in the next step. This instance stores it encrypted, but its operator can still use it.

self.expiredHelp: This setup code has expired. Click New code, then copy the command again.

pairs.noGuild: Choose the Discord server to bridge first. Its channels show up here after that.
pairs.lead: Each pair links one channel here with one channel in {guild}.
pairs.discordGoneFix: The bot can no longer find this Discord channel: it was deleted, or the bot lost access to it. Remove the pair, or give the bot access again.

not_visible.fix: In Discord, right-click {channel} → Edit Channel → Permissions. Add the bot (or its role) and allow View Channel and Read Message History.

cannot_send.fix: In Discord, right-click {channel} → Edit Channel → Permissions, and allow Send Messages for the bot.

cannot_manage_webhooks.fix: Messages from Harmony arrive under the bot's name instead of each sender's name and picture. To fix it, allow Manage Webhooks for the bot in the permissions of {channel}.

match.lead: These channels have the same name on both sides. Pair them all at once, both ways?

pairs.noDiscordLeft: The bot sees no unpaired text channels in {guild}. Give the bot access to more channels in Discord; this list updates by itself.

validation.blocked: The bot can't use {channel} yet. Fix its permissions in Discord first, as described above.

pairs.fromDiscord: You can also pair from Discord with {command}. It asks for the Harmony channel's ID: right-click the channel here and choose {copyId}.

maintain.self: Move the bridge to another computer, or reinstall it
maintain.instance: Re-link the bot, or link a different Discord server

disconnectBody.self: Stops bridging and removes all channel pairs and the bridge's Harmony bot. Messages that were already bridged stay. Your Discord bot isn't deleted; remove it in the Developer Portal if you no longer need it.
disconnectBody.hosted: Stops bridging, removes all channel pairs and the bridge's Harmony bot, and deletes the stored Discord token. Messages that were already bridged stay. Your Discord bot isn't deleted; remove it in the Developer Portal if you no longer need it.
disconnectBody.instance: Stops bridging and removes all channel pairs and the bridge's Harmony bot. Messages that were already bridged stay. The bot leaves your Discord server by itself within about ten minutes.

disconnect.title: Disconnect the bridge?
disconnect.message: Bridging stops right away and every channel pair is removed. This can't be undone; to bridge again you set it up from the start.

startOver.title: Start over?
startOver.message: This removes the bridge you started setting up, so you can choose again.

confirm.selfNote: Also stop the program on your computer: {command}
confirm.instanceNote: This instance's bot leaves your Discord server by itself within about ten minutes. There is nothing to remove in Discord.

bridge_offline.title: The bridge is offline.
bridge_offline.fixSelf: Make sure the computer running it is on and Docker is running, then start the bridge with the first command below. If it stops again, the second command shows why.
bridge_offline.fixHosted: This instance isn't running your bridge right now. Wait a few minutes; if it stays offline, contact the instance's admin.
bridge_offline.fixInstance: This instance isn't running your bridge right now. Wait a few minutes; if it stays offline, contact the instance's admin.

discord_token_invalid.title: Discord rejected the bot token.
discord_token_invalid.fixSelf: In the Developer Portal, open your application → Bot → Reset Token and copy the new token. Remove the old bridge with the command below, then run the setup command again with the new token. The bridge remembers its Harmony sign-in.
discord_token_invalid.fixHosted: In the Developer Portal, open your application → Bot → Reset Token, copy the new token and save it here.
discord_token_invalid.fixInstance: This is on the instance's side: its bot needs a new token. Contact the instance's admin.

intent_missing.title: Discord refused the {intent}.
intent_missing.fixSelf: In the Developer Portal, open your application → Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents, switch on {intent} and click Save Changes. Then restart the bridge with the command below.
intent_missing.fixHosted: In the Developer Portal, open your application → Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents, switch on {intent} and click Save Changes. The bridge picks it up when it reconnects, within a few minutes.
intent_missing.fixInstance: This instance's bot doesn't have the {intent}. Turn off the option that needs it, or ask the instance's admin.

bot_not_in_guild.title: The bot isn't in {guild}.
bot_not_in_guild.fix: Use “Invite the bot to your Discord server” (you need the Manage Server permission there), or choose another Discord server.
bot_not_in_guild.fixInstance: The bot was removed from {guild}. Add it to Discord again to keep bridging.

no_guild.title: The bot isn't in any Discord server yet.
no_guild.fix: Use “Invite the bot to your Discord server” and pick your server in the Discord window that opens. You need the Manage Server permission there.
no_guild.fixInstance: Add the bot to your Discord server again.

guild_not_selected.title: No Discord server chosen yet.
guild_not_selected.fix: Choose which Discord server to bridge.
guild_not_selected.fixInstance: Add the bot to your Discord server to link it.

channel_not_visible.title: The bot can't see {channel}.
channel_not_visible.fix: In Discord, right-click {channel} → Edit Channel → Permissions. Add the bot (or its role) and allow View Channel and Read Message History.

cannot_send.title: The bot can't post in {channel}.
cannot_send.fix: In Discord, right-click {channel} → Edit Channel → Permissions, and allow Send Messages for the bot.

cannot_manage_webhooks.title: The bot can't manage webhooks in {channel}.
cannot_manage_webhooks.fix: Messages from Harmony arrive under the bot's name instead of each sender's name and picture. To fix it, allow Manage Webhooks for the bot in the channel's permissions.

harmony_auth_failed.title: The bridge can no longer sign in to Harmony.
harmony_auth_failed.fixSelf: Reset the bridge with the command below, then run the setup command again with a new setup code.
harmony_auth_failed.fixHosted: This is on the instance's side. Contact the instance's admin. If it keeps failing, disconnect the bridge below and set it up again.
harmony_auth_failed.fixInstance: This is on the instance's side. Contact the instance's admin. If it keeps failing, disconnect the bridge below and set it up again.

harmony_channel_missing.title: A paired Harmony channel no longer exists.
harmony_channel_missing.fix: Remove its pair from the paired channels.

harmony_channel_encrypted.title: {channel} is end-to-end encrypted, so the bridge can't read it.
harmony_channel_encrypted.fix: Remove that pair and pair a channel without end-to-end encryption instead.

rate_limited.title: Discord is slowing the bridge down.
rate_limited.fix: Nothing to do: messages are delayed, not lost. If it keeps happening, turn off presence sync or member list sync.

discord_unreachable.title: The bridge can't reach Discord.
discord_unreachable.fixSelf: Check that the computer running the bridge is online. If Discord itself is down, the bridge reconnects once it's back.
discord_unreachable.fixHosted: Discord may be down, or this instance has network trouble. The bridge keeps retrying; if it lasts, contact the instance's admin.
discord_unreachable.fixInstance: Discord may be down, or this instance has network trouble. The bridge keeps retrying; if it lasts, contact the instance's admin.

harmony_unreachable.title: The bridge can't reach this Harmony instance.
harmony_unreachable.fixSelf: Check that the computer running the bridge can open {url}. The bridge keeps retrying.
harmony_unreachable.fixHosted: This is on the instance's side, and the bridge keeps retrying. If it lasts, contact the instance's admin.
harmony_unreachable.fixInstance: This is on the instance's side, and the bridge keeps retrying. If it lasts, contact the instance's admin.

upgrade.doubleRelay: Once the new bridge works, stop the old bridge program, or every message gets copied twice.

botGuide.title: Discord bridge
botGuide.managed: This bot is the Discord bridge of {server}. It is set up and managed there; there is nothing to configure here.
botGuide.unmanaged: Discord bridges are set up from a server's settings: Server Settings → Discord Bridge. That page creates and manages the bridge's bot for you, so you don't need to create one here.
botGuide.legacyTitle: Manual setup for the old bridge (v1)
botGuide.legacyLead: Only for the old harmony-discord-bridge program that reads a config file.
botGuide.harmonyPermissions: Add this bot to the server with Read Messages and Send Messages (and Manage Channels for /bridge clone-server).
botGuide.intents: Discord intents: {messageContent} is required; {members} only if the bridge syncs the member list; {presence} only if presence sync is on.
botGuide.invite: Paste your Discord application's ID (General Information → Application ID) to get an invite link.

adminSection.title: Discord bridge
adminSection.lead: Communities connect a Discord server in Server Settings → Discord Bridge. Offer them this instance's bot, let them bring their own, or both. Running the bridge on a computer of their own is always possible.

admin.title: Let communities bring their own bot
admin.lead: Communities create their own Discord bot, with their own name and avatar, and paste its token; this instance runs it. Server admins see this as “Use your own bot, run on this instance”.
admin.toggleHint: You hold each community's Discord bot token. A token gives access to every Discord channel its bot can see.
admin.limitHint: New hosted bridges are refused once this many exist. Existing ones keep running.
admin.limitInvalid: Enter a whole number, 0 or more.
admin.note: Turning this on only offers the option. You also need to run the bridge host service ({service}) next to this instance; see the {docs}.
admin.saveFailed: Couldn't save the bridge hosting settings
admin.loadFailed: Couldn't load the bridge hosting settings.

instance.lead: This instance's Discord bot does the bridging. Add it to your Discord server: Discord asks which server and shows what the bot may do there.
instance.step2: Pick your Discord server (you need the Manage Server permission there) and click {authorize}.
instance.step3: Discord sends you back here to pair channels.
instance.privacy: The bot belongs to this instance's operator, who can read every Discord channel the bot has access to. Give it access only to the channels you bridge.
instance.relink: The bridge is linked to {guild}. Adding the bot to {guild} again keeps the channel pairs and grants the permissions an older link lacks, such as Manage Messages: without it, a Discord member's message deleted here stays on Discord. Adding the bot to another Discord server moves the bridge there and removes the channel pairs; the bot leaves {guild} by itself within about ten minutes.
instance.linked: Linked to {guild}. Now pair the channels.

linkError.discord_denied: The bot wasn't added: the request was cancelled in Discord. Click Try again and choose Authorize.
linkError.exchange_failed: Discord didn't confirm the link. Try again in a moment; if it keeps failing, contact the instance's admin.
linkError.limit_reached: This instance's bot is already in as many Discord servers as it allows. Ask the instance's admin, or use a Discord bot of your own instead.

instanceAdmin.lead: One public Discord bot run by this instance. Communities add it to their Discord server in one click instead of creating a bot of their own, and this instance runs their bridges.

portal.title: Set up the bot in the Discord Developer Portal
portal.create: Open the {portal} and click {newApplication}. Name it, for example {example}, accept Discord's terms and click {create}.
portal.applicationId: On {generalInformation}, copy the {applicationId} into the field below.
portal.codeGrantWhy: With the code grant on, the bot joins a Discord server only when a community links it from Harmony.
portal.intents: Under {section}, switch on {messageContent} and {members}. Switch on {presence} only if you turn on presence sync below. Click {save}.
portal.token: Click {reset}, then {copy}, and paste the token into {field} below.
portal.redirect: Open {oauth2}. Under {redirects}, click {addRedirect}, paste this address and click {save}:
portal.redirectExact: It has to match exactly, including https and the path.
portal.secret: Still in {oauth2}, click {resetSecret} under {clientSecret}, copy it and paste it into {field} below.
portal.finish: Save the credentials below, then switch on “Offer this bot to communities”.
portal.verification: Discord limits a bot to 100 servers until it is verified. Before that, apply for verification in the Developer Portal (App Verification) and request the Message Content and Server Members intents, and the Presence intent if you use presence sync. Discord rarely grants Presence.

instanceAdmin.appIdInvalid: An Application ID is a number of 17 to 20 digits.
instanceAdmin.keepPlaceholder: Stored. Leave empty to keep it.
instanceAdmin.writeOnly: Secrets are stored encrypted and never shown again. Paste a new value only to replace one.
instanceAdmin.secretIsToken: That's the bot token. The client secret is under OAuth2 → Client Secret.
instanceAdmin.secretInvalid: That doesn't look like a client secret. Copy it from OAuth2 → Client Secret.
instanceAdmin.clearConfirm: Remove the bot's credentials? Linked communities stop bridging until a bot is set up again. Their bridges and channel pairs stay.
instanceAdmin.enableHint: Server admins see “Use this instance's bot” first in Server Settings → Discord Bridge.
instanceAdmin.enableNeedsConfig: Save the Application ID, client secret and bot token first.
instanceAdmin.presenceHint: Requests Discord's Presence intent for every linked server, so communities can show who is online. Only changes of status are sent. Turn it on only while the Presence intent is on in the Developer Portal; past 100 servers, Discord has to approve it.
instanceAdmin.limitHint: New links are refused once this many Discord servers are linked. Discord allows 100 until the bot is verified.
instanceAdmin.hostNote: Linked servers are bridged by the bridge host service ({service}, bridge 2.1.0 or later) next to this instance; see the {docs}.
